extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines for creating and evaluating a stand-up joke's premise, point of view/angle, and punch line so the joke follows a clear setup–development–twist structure. Focused on crafting topic + condition + POV that lead efficiently to a surprising punch.

rubrics_metrics.name: Universal Joke Formula
rubrics_metrics.description: Premise + Point of View + Twist = Joke
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the page's core formula: a joke should combine a clear premise, a specific point of view (angle), and a twist/punch to produce humor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Premise (topic + weird/crazy/difficult/stupid)
rubrics_metrics.description: The topic or what your joke is about. Found by asking yourself what is weird, crazy, difficult, or stupid about your topic.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A strong premise highlights something odd or problematic about a concrete subject; the page emphasizes locating 'weird, crazy, difficult, or stupid' aspects of the topic.

rubrics_metrics.name: Topic (concrete subject matter)
rubrics_metrics.description: The subject matter — concrete object, experience, person, situation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pick a concrete, specific target for the joke (an experience, object, or person) rather than an abstract idea, so the audience can picture it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Condition (setting/situation/POV)
rubrics_metrics.description: A premise = topic + condition. A condition could be a setting, situation, or POV.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Add a setting or perspective to a topic to create a premise (for example, 'in New York' or 'as a new parent'); the condition narrows the topic into a joke-ready setup.

rubrics_metrics.name: Point of View (specific perspective)
rubrics_metrics.description: The specific point of view from which the premise is observed or delivered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The formula explicitly requires a point of view; the rubric later asks 'Is there a specific point of view?' — a consistent, specific POV helps direct the audience's assumptions and makes the twist land.

rubrics_metrics.name: Angle (connective tissue between topic and punch line)
rubrics_metrics.description: The connective tissue between Topic and Punch Line. Smooth and efficient.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The angle links setup to punch; it should be concise and guide the audience from the premise toward the expectation that the punch will subvert.

rubrics_metrics.name: Punch Line (twist that breaks assumptions)
rubrics_metrics.description: The twist that breaks the assumption built up in setup.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The punch should break a built assumption; it must be a surprise relative to the set-up and angle while feeling earned by what came before.

rubrics_metrics.name: "It was SO X that __" template
rubrics_metrics.description: "It was SO X that __" — superlative sets up extreme; punch lists the absurd consequence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: 'My apartment was so quiet that I thought the flies were studying.' Use an extreme descriptor to justify an absurd, specific consequence as the punch.

rubrics_metrics.name: "But" statements template
rubrics_metrics.description: "But Statements" — start with the normal assumption, add 'but,' end with the inappropriate / weird / broken assumption.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Frame a familiar sentiment then immediately undercut it: e.g., 'I love my job, but I'd love it more if I weren't there.' Use the 'but' to pivot into the unexpected.

rubrics_metrics.name: "Have you ever noticed…?" opener
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow this opener with a specific, oddly truthful detail that reframes a common experience into something comic and particular.

rubrics_metrics.name: "What's the deal with…?" opener
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this to frame a target for examination; the question signals the comedian will point out the incongruity or absurdity in a common thing or behavior.

rubrics_metrics.name: Joke Arc: Beginning / Middle / End (setup/angle/punch)
rubrics_metrics.description: Joke has a beginning (setup / premise), middle (angle / development), and end (punch / twist), like an essay.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure the joke progresses logically: establish the premise, develop it with a clear angle that cultivates an expectation, then release that expectation with a twist. The rubric asks whether you can state the joke in setup-angle-punch form.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rubric item: Is the premise clear (topic + weird/crazy/etc.)?
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluation: Is the premise clear (topic + weird/crazy/etc.)?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check that the audience can identify the topic and the odd condition or problem that makes it funny; ambiguity weakens the joke's foundation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rubric item: Is there a specific point of view?
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluation: Is there a specific point of view?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Confirm the joke adopts a distinct POV (persona, narrator stance, or vantage) that shapes how the premise is presented and how the punch reads.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rubric item: Is there a clean angle linking topic to punch?
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluation: Is there a clean angle linking topic to punch?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether the angle smoothly and efficiently connects the setup to the punch; a messy or extraneous angle will dilute the payoff.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rubric item: Does the punch break a built assumption?
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluation: Does the punch break a built assumption?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The punch should violate an expectation that the setup and angle created; if the punch merely restates or strengthens the assumption, it won't be funny.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rubric item: Could you state the joke in setup-angle-punch form?
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluation: Could you state the joke in setup-angle-punch form?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A concise articulation in this form indicates structural clarity. If you cannot distill the joke to these three parts, it's likely unfocused and needs tightening.
